title: Pre-Analysis — Wear Pin Datum Standard Against the Taxi Duty Proposal
abstract: Closed work order asking whether the wear pin datum standard would still be valid if the heat stack changed, and delegating the wear scale question to the taxi duty candidate.

sections.objective: Establish what the wear pin datum standard assumes about the heat stack, in support of a proposal to change to an oxidation-inhibited carbon grade for airports where taxi energy rather than landing energy consumes the stack. The specific question was whether the relocated datum and its millimetre scale survive a change of usable stack thickness.
sections.findings_summary: The datum survives; the scale does not. Moving the reading to the torque tube flange made it independent of the pressure plate, which is what the standard was for, and a different carbon grade does not affect that. But the usable stack thickness changes by four millimetres with the new grade, so the millimetre scale has to be re-marked and the acceptance table reissued. That leaves three acceptance tables in circulation during the transition, which is one more than the wear measurement task can currently express, and mixing standards on a bogie is already prohibited for the same reason. The trouble shooting procedure for an inconsistent wear reading is written around two datum standards and would need a third case. None of this obstructs the proposal; it is all documentation, and it belongs with the candidate rather than here.
sections.next_steps: Delegate the scale and acceptance table work to the taxi duty candidate. Confirm to that team that the datum standard is a prerequisite and must be embodied first. Recommend that the transition period be planned so that no operator holds three tables at once.

tasks.title: Establish what the relocated datum depends on
Assess the acceptance table count during transition
Check the trouble shooting procedure coverage

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the brake regulator and collar part numbers the task calls out.

expected_findings.rationale: The wear measurement task carries two acceptance tables selected by datum standard. A third carbon grade adds a third table on the same datum, which the task structure cannot express without a second selector.
expected_findings.resolution: Restructure the task selector as part of the candidate rather than as a separate change.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the brake regulator and pump part numbers the procedure names.

expected_findings.rationale: The inconsistent reading procedure is written around two datum standards and its final caution says not to compare readings across them. A third grade on the same datum makes that caution insufficient.
expected_findings.resolution: Extend the procedure with the third case when the candidate is embodied.

evidence.similarity_note: Reached from the modification to its retrofit bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The retrofit bulletin is the vehicle for the datum standard and will become a prerequisite for the taxi duty candidate rather than a competitor to it. Its compliance wording does not currently anticipate being a prerequisite.
expected_findings.resolution: Restate the bulletin as a prerequisite when the candidate bulletin is issued.

type_data.conclusion: Closed and delegated. The datum survives the grade change; the scale and the tables do not.
